analyticalMisses.summary: Milwaukee model probability (~72%) was too far above the Kalshi market (~62-63%) and sharp-market (~61-62%) probability without sufficient independent justification for the divergence; Milwaukee lost 8-6 after leading 4-0.
Both YRFI losses exposed excessive reliance on full-game/proxy pitcher and lineup inputs in place of first-inning-specific data; COL-STL and LAD-ARI were both 0-0 after the first inning.

analyticalWins.summary: Washington starter-matchup thesis (Cavalli vs. Petty) was the strongest process and result of the slate; Washington won 5-3.
Yankees full-game ML was a cleaner expression of the thesis than a three-way F5 team contract, avoiding tie risk while retaining the bullpen thesis; Yankees won 3-2.

processErrors.summary: User-facing Kalshi American odds were derived from midpoint probability instead of the executable YES ask on all five bets.
The manual handicap was overly anchored to slate/model projections rather than an independently-established fair probability, particularly on large model/market disagreements.
First-inning (YRFI) recommendations were allowed despite the pregame slate explicitly lacking first-inning-specific xERA/splits inputs.

proposedInvestigations.summary: Audit every recommendation/output path that creates the user-facing "current American odds" field to ensure it uses executable YES ask rather than midpoint.
Audit bet-up-to enforcement for the same midpoint-vs-ask issue.
Preserve bid / ask / midpoint / last as distinct archived fields for research and CLV analysis.
Determine whether historical recommended-price fields need an explicit priceBasis (EXECUTABLE_ASK, MIDPOINT, LAST, or VIG_FREE).
Review YRFI/NRFI qualification criteria when first-inning-specific data is unavailable.
Review large model-versus-sharp-market divergences (>7 percentage points) to determine whether an additional real-money confirmation gate is warranted.
Continue the ticker-mapping cleanup so every pipeline market key maps to the exact archived Kalshi ticker, with field states distinguishing not_applicable, not_computed, and parser_unresolved.
